messages:
maria: Quick async check — we're planning to deprecate the legacy `tool_call` ordering in chat/completions. Before I open the PR: does anyone expect downstream clients to rely on a deterministic order of `tool_call.args` across streaming deltas?
aj: short answer: some internal SDKs do rely on stable ordering in the assembled delta stream. We should avoid a hard break. Can we provide an explicit ordering field instead of changing semantics? :thinking_face: 
maria: what's the minimal compatibility surface we can keep? i.e., keep current ordering for N months and emit a migration warning?
jordan: agree w/ aj. Proposal: add `tool_call.seq` (int) per fragment in streaming deltas and keep current behavior for assembly. Clients that reconstruct messages should use `seq` when present. That lets us reorder internal fragments later.
sree: small nit — we'll need to guarantee `seq` monotonicity across reconnects. Also runtime needs to include a per-connection epoch so fragments from prior connections aren't mixed. Suggest `seq` + `conn_id`.
aj: yeah conn_id makes sense. Example streaming fragment we can standardize on: ```json\n{\n  "type": "delta",\n  "conn_id": "abc123",\n  "seq": 12,\n  "tool_call": {"name": "search", "args": ["q=foo"]}\n}\n``` 
maria: perfect. Two questions: 1) how do we expose this in the non-streaming (sync) JSON shape so sync clients can validate? 2) rollout plan?
olivia: for sync responses we can include a top-level `tool_call_ordering` object: `{"strategy":"seq","conn_id":null}` — mostly to help schema validators and lint rules. No change to existing `tool_call` shape.
jordan: rollout: feature flag behind `streaming_seq` on Dedicated/Hosted. Default off for 6 weeks, opt-in via header `X-Redwood-Streaming: seq-v1`. After opt-in period, flip default and keep old behavior for customers with `legacy_streaming=true` until contract deprecation window ends.
maria: sounds good. aj — can you add a request in the SDK repo to prefer `seq` if present? quick PR + tests?
aj: yep, i'll open PR tomorrow. will add tests for reconnect ordering too.
sree: runtime side: i'll ensure conn_id in proxies and in runtime tracing. hooking up tracing tags so we can audit out-of-order fragments. putting a canary in us-west first.
maria: pinging on code review: @aj whenever you open the SDK PR, can you drop a link here so i can include it in the contract change doc? also i'll add a short migration note for customers.
dev-bot: CI passed for branch add/streaming-seq (build 4821) :white_check_mark:
aj: PR opened: https://git.internal/rw/sdk/pull/842 — includes seq handling + tests. cc @maria
maria: thanks — i'll draft the contract RFC and include the rollout timeline. Let's also add a lint rule in `redwood-contracts` that flags missing `tool_call.seq` in streaming fragments once the header is enabled.
jordan: one more runtime concern: fallback behavior for legacy models that don't emit seq. We should: 1) accept stream (no seq) and mark connection as legacy, 2) avoid mixing legacy and seq fragments in same assembled call (drop warning). That keeps reliability.
maria: agreed. i'll add those constraints to the RFC. If no objections i'll merge RFC by EOD and schedule the canary rollout next Tues.
olivia: no objections from product. :+1:
maria: thanks team — follow-ups: aj PR link, jordan/runtimes confirm canary target, sree add tracing tags. i'll post RFC link once merged.
